deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a draft of a lecture announcement (Vorlesungsankündigung) for the Göttingen lecture catalogue, written first in Latin and then in German. It is headed 'Riemann 3' and has an archival folio number 62 in the margin.

Latin draft, with corrections resolved: 'Riemann, Dr. privatim theoriam gravitatis, magnetismi et electricitatis mathematicam docebit Lun. Mart. Merc. & Jov. h. IX[-X]; publice methodum quadratorum minimorum binis scholis h. V-VI.' The deleted and replaced words show the drafting process:
- An initial title (read as 'Professor') is struck.
- The weekdays are revised from Lun./Mart./Jov./Ven. to Lun./Mart./Merc./Jov.
- A word before 'methodum' (read as 'Gratuitus') is replaced by 'publice'.
- 'exponet' is struck.

German draft: 'Die mathematische Theorie der Schwere, des Magnetismus und der Electricität Mo. Dienst. Mittw. u. Donnerst. v. 9-10 Uhr; öffentlich Methode der kleinsten Quadrate zweimal wöchentlich v. 5-6 Uhr.' Its opening words ('Prof. Riemann wird') and the verb 'vortragen' are struck.

So the planned teaching is:
- a private course, four hours a week, on the mathematical theory of gravitation, electricity and magnetism;
- a free public course, two hours a week, on the method of least squares.

The gravitation, electricity and magnetism course corresponds to the lectures later edited by K. Hattendorff ('Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus', 1876). Riemann gave them in the early 1860s; the summer semester of 1861 is the usual date, though the exact semester of this draft is not determinable from the page alone.

The sheet's presence in the 'Primzahlen' bundle is incidental. The neighbouring pages concern the zeta function (previous page) and a letter draft on the Dirichlet principle (next page). There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: No mathematical content, hence no mathematical errors. One minor internal point: the Latin hour, written 'h. IX' with an overwritten or struck numeral, should correspond to the German 'v. 9-10 Uhr'. The two versions agree if the hour is read as IX (that is, IX-X).

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative draft of a lecture-catalogue entry with no mathematics. Riemann's lecture courses on gravity, electricity and magnetism are well documented, and announcing a least-squares course was standard in Göttingen after Gauss.
transcription_corrections: The deleted word before 'Riemann, Dr.' in the Latin line looks like 'Professor' (abbreviated or struck); the reading is uncertain.
'[-Hebd.-]' is uncertain. The struck word before 'Lun.' could be an abbreviation such as 'Diebb.'/'Hebd.'; it is illegible in detail.
The hour in the Latin line reads 'h. IX' with corrections (an overwritten IX/X). Given the German '9-10 Uhr', 'h. IX' (i.e. IX-X) is the intended reading rather than 'X'.
The struck word before '{+publice+}' may be 'Gratuito' or 'Gratis' rather than 'Gratuitus'; it is uncertain.
'binis scholis' (twice weekly) is correct, matching the German 'zweimal wöchentlich'.
The German line ends 'Methode der kleinsten Quadrate zweimal wöchentlich v. 5-6 Uhr'; 'zwei-/mal' is hyphenated across the line break.
